  <section class="rule-section applied-intro">

      FIELD GUIDE / APPLIED MATHEMATICS
    </div>

    <h1 class="interior-title">
      THINKING<br>
      ABOUT<br>
      APPLIED MATH?
    </h1>

    <p class="dek">
      If you like patterns, models, computation, proofs,
      networks, differential equations, or figuring out why
      complicated systems behave the way they do, you may
      already be thinking like an applied mathematician.
    </p>

  </section>


  <!-- =====================================================
       WHAT IS IT?
       ===================================================== -->

  <section class="rule-section split applied-section">

    <div>

      <div class="fig-label">
        01 / WHAT IS APPLIED MATH?
      </div>

      <h2>
        MATH THAT<br>
        HAS SOMEWHERE<br>
        TO GO.
      </h2>

    </div>


    <div class="body-copy">

      <p>
        Applied mathematics is about using mathematical ideas
        to understand systems, make predictions, uncover structure,
        and solve problems.
      </p>

      <p>
        Sometimes the problem comes from physics, biology,
        engineering, computing, economics, or data.
        Sometimes the mathematics becomes interesting enough
        that the original application is almost beside the point.
      </p>

    </div>

  </section>


  <!-- =====================================================
       WHAT DO YOU STUDY?
       ===================================================== -->

  <div class="applied-topics">

  <div class="applied-topic">
    <div class="applied-topic-number">01</div>
    <h3>Modeling</h3>
    <p>
      Take a messy real-world system and turn it into mathematics
      you can analyze, test, and improve.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="applied-topic">
    <div class="applied-topic-number">02</div>
    <h3>Computation</h3>
    <p>
      Build numerical methods, simulations, and algorithms for
      problems that do not have neat closed-form answers.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="applied-topic">
    <div class="applied-topic-number">03</div>
    <h3>Dynamical Systems</h3>
    <p>
      Use differential equations to understand systems that evolve:
      populations, circuits, motion, interacting components, and more.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="applied-topic">
    <div class="applied-topic-number">04</div>
    <h3>Discrete Structures</h3>
    <p>
      Study graphs, networks, combinatorics, algorithms, and the
      mathematics of systems made from connected pieces.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="applied-topic">
    <div class="applied-topic-number">05</div>
    <h3>Randomness + Uncertainty</h3>
    <p>
      Work with probability, stochastic systems, uncertainty
      quantification, and models where the outcome is not predetermined.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="applied-topic">
    <div class="applied-topic-number">06</div>
    <h3>Analysis + Optimization</h3>
    <p>
      Ask what solutions exist, how systems behave, and how to find
      the best possible choice under competing constraints.
    </p>
  </div>

</div>
